topic: Prestressed concrete: pre-tensioning, post-tensioning, tendons, losses
source: 601-80.json, 681-760.json, 761-842.json, Concrete_1-50.json, Concrete_101-150.json, Concrete_151-200.json, Concrete_50-100.json, conc_201-250.json, conc_250-300.json, conc_301-350.json, conc_350-405.json

questions.q: 345. Prestress is imparted to concrete by bearing in
questions.explain: In post-tensioning, the prestressing force is transferred to the concrete through end anchorages bearing against the concrete member, unlike pre-tensioning where it is transferred by bond.

questions.q: 346. The minimum grade of concrete for pre-tensioned member is
questions.explain: Pre-tensioned members require high early strength to allow release of the tendons, so a minimum grade of M40 concrete is specified.

questions.q: 347. The mix proportion of cement mortar to be used in the joints in precast prestressed member is
questions.explain: A relatively rich mortar mix of 1:1.5 (cement:sand) is recommended for filling joints between precast prestressed concrete units to ensure adequate strength and durability.

questions.q: 348. The diameter of high tensile steel tendons used is
questions.explain: High tensile steel wires used as tendons in prestressed concrete typically range from about 5 mm to 8 mm in diameter.

questions.q: 349. The minimum clear spacing for single wires used in pre-tension system is
options: 2 times the diameter of the wire and max. size of aggregate whichever is greater
3 times the diameter of the wire and max. size of aggregate whichever is greater
2 times the diameter of the wire and 1.5 times max. size of aggregate whichever is greater
3 times the diameter of the wire and 1.5 times max. size of aggregate whichever is greater
questions.explain: IS code requires the minimum clear spacing between single pre-tensioned wires to be the greater of 3 times the wire diameter or 1.5 times the maximum aggregate size, to ensure proper compaction and bond.

questions.q: 350. The minimum clear spacing of non-grouped cables or large bars shall be
options: maximum size of cable or bar
5 mm plus maximum size of aggregate
questions.explain: The code specifies the minimum clear spacing for non-grouped cables/large bars as whichever is greatest among 40 mm, the cable/bar size, or 5 mm plus the maximum aggregate size.

questions.q: 351. The minimum clear horizontal spacing between groups of cables or ducts of grouped cables shall be greater of
options: 30 mm or 5 mm more than maximum size of aggregate
40 mm or 5 mm more than maximum size of aggregate
30 mm or maximum size of aggregate
40 mm or maximum size of aggregate
questions.explain: The code requires the minimum clear horizontal spacing between groups/ducts of grouped cables to be the greater of 40 mm or 5 mm more than the maximum aggregate size, to permit proper concrete placement.

questions.q: 352. The minimum clear vertical spacing between groups of cables or ducts of grouped cables shall be
questions.explain: For grouped cables/ducts, the code specifies a minimum clear vertical spacing of 50 mm between groups to ensure adequate concrete cover and compaction.

questions.q: 353. The grouting of ducts in post-tensioned prestressed concrete causes
questions.explain: Grouting bonds the tendon to the surrounding concrete, which improves load transfer (reducing deflection and crack width) while also protecting the tendon from corrosion — all benefits occur together.

questions.q: 354. A parabolic tendon in prestressed beam causes an equivalent balancing
questions.explain: A parabolic tendon profile produces a uniformly varying upward transverse force along its length, which acts as an equivalent distributed load balancing the external gravity loads on the beam.

questions.q: 357. In case of prestressed concrete, prestressing force is
questions.explain: Prestressing induces a compressive force in the concrete section (via tensioned tendons) so that tensile stresses from external loads are counteracted.

questions.q: 358. In case of prestressed concrete
options: load carrying capacity of member increases
quantity of concrete is saved for same grade
quantity of steel is saved for same grade
questions.explain: Prestressing utilizes the full section more efficiently, so it increases load-carrying capacity while also economizing on both concrete and steel quantities compared to ordinary RCC — all these benefits occur.

questions.q: 378. The purpose of reinforcement in prestressed concrete is :
options: to impact initial compressive stress in concrete
questions.explain: The prestressing steel is tensioned specifically to impart an initial compressive stress into the concrete section before service loads are applied, which is the primary purpose in prestressed members.

questions.q: 388. For the same design load, the weight of concrete in a prestressed concrete as compared to ordinary reinforced concrete is less by :
questions.explain: Because prestressed members use the full section more efficiently by pre-compressing the concrete, they require considerably less concrete — typically about 50% less — than an equivalent ordinary RCC member for the same load.

questions.q: 5. Ferro-concrete is another name given to (Ferror = iron)
questions.explain: Ferro-concrete literally means iron-concrete, referring to concrete reinforced with steel (iron) bars, i.e., reinforced cement concrete.

questions.q: 7. The cement concrete in which high compressive stressed are artificially induced before its actual use, is called
questions.explain: Prestressed concrete has internal compressive stresses artificially induced (via tensioned tendons) before loading, so that tensile stresses from service loads are offset.

questions.q: 8. The cement concrete, from which entrained air and excess water are removed after placing it in position, is called
questions.explain: In vacuum concrete, a vacuum process is applied after placing to remove excess water and entrapped air, increasing density and early strength.

questions.q: 184. Cube strength of controlled concrete to be used for pretensioned and post-tensioned work respectively should not be less than
questions.explain: For prestressed concrete work, the required minimum cube strengths differ for pretensioned (420 kg/cm²) and post-tensioned (350 kg/cm²) systems due to their different stress transfer mechanisms.

questions.q: 224. The minimum grade of concrete prescribed for prestressed construction is
questions.explain: Prestressed concrete construction requires higher strength concrete to handle prestressing forces, with a minimum grade of M40 prescribed for pre-tensioned systems.

questions.q: 228. The cement concrete in which high compressive stressed are artificially induced before its actual use is called
questions.explain: Prestressed concrete has compressive stresses artificially induced through tensioned tendons before the structure is put into service, to counteract future tensile stresses.

questions.q: 238. The major loss of prestressed concrete is caused due to
questions.explain: Prestress losses in prestressed concrete occur due to a combination of factors: creep of concrete, relaxation of steel tendons, and shrinkage of concrete, all contributing together.
